types.necessity: L1.identity requires that a change to a trade does not make it a different trade; a value invariant across every report of the same trade is required to express that persistence, which is exactly the identity mutation role.
types.parallel_assumption: Credible while the brokerage's trade number is never reassigned to a different trade; if a trade number were reused for a different trade this role would misidentify reports, which should trigger review.
types.review_trigger: the same trade_number value appears to identify two trades the business considers different

types.necessity: L1.attribution-at-placement requires a trade to belong to the account it was placed under, and requires that a later change does not move a trade that was already placed; a value naming that account, set once and never replaced by a later report, is required to express that. L1.identity supplies the account's own persistent number as the value this reference carries.
types.parallel_assumption: Credible while a trade's account assignment is settled at the trade's first-encountered report and never legitimately contradicted by a later report of the same trade.
types.review_trigger: a later report of a known trade names an account different from the one recorded at first encounter

types.necessity: L1.placement-moment requires the trade's placement to be the moment stated by the earliest report of it the brokerage holds, in that report's own recorded time. L1.attribution-at-placement requires that a later change does not move a trade that was already placed; since this moment is what selects the account statement the trade references, it must be set once and never replaced, or a later report could shift which statement is selected and move the trade's ownership.
types.parallel_assumption: Credible while the earliest report of a trade the brokerage holds states its own time, and that time is treated as the placement moment even when it is not the trade's true first lifecycle event (the first-seen-late case L1.placement-moment names).
types.review_trigger: a trade's first-encountered report carries no determinable event time

types.necessity: L1.attribution-at-placement requires the trade's ownership to reference the account as it stood at placement, not merely which account; L1.as-of defines that answer as the account's statement whose effective_from is the latest at or before the queried moment; a dedicated value carrying that specific effective_from is required to complete the (account_number, effective_from) reference that identifies the exact account statement. L1.lifecycle-mutates-outcome states directly that a later report of the same trade 'leaves the ownership as first recorded'; on this entity (incremental_by_identity, not versioned), that reference is fixed once at first encounter and never replaced by a later report, which is exactly the frozen_from_first_encounter role -- not per_statement, which describes a value's own kept-history nature on a versioned entity, a role that belongs to the account entity this value is drawn from, not to how it behaves once pinned here.
types.parallel_assumption: Credible while the upstream logical.account entity carries a statement of this trade's owning account whose effective_from is at or before placed_at.
types.review_trigger: no logical.account statement of the trade's owning account has an effective_from at or before placed_at

types.necessity: L1.attribution-at-placement requires that, through the account, the trade also belongs to the customer as that customer stood at the same moment; a dedicated value naming that customer is required to express that half of the clause. L1.lifecycle-mutates-outcome states directly that a later report of the same trade 'leaves the ownership as first recorded'; on this entity (incremental_by_identity, not versioned), that customer reference is fixed once at first encounter and never replaced by a later report, which is exactly the frozen_from_first_encounter role -- not per_statement, which describes the value's own kept-history nature on the account entity it is drawn from, not how it behaves once pinned here.
types.parallel_assumption: Credible while the account statement this trade's ownership pins has a resolvable owning customer.
types.review_trigger: the account statement this trade's ownership pins has no resolvable owning customer

types.necessity: L1.placement-moment requires a trade whose first-encountered report is not its true earliest lifecycle report to be marked first seen late, so the ownership placement fixes can be reviewed; a dedicated value carrying that marking is required to express it. L1.attribution-at-placement's 'do not move a trade that was already placed' requires this marking, once made at first encounter, never to be reconsidered by a later report -- frozen_from_first_encounter, not mutable.
types.parallel_assumption: Credible while the anchored trade_code_meanings.status_order and report_order let this job determine, at first encounter, whether the trade's lifecycle appears to have started before that report.
types.review_trigger: a trade's first-encountered report carries a status outside the anchored status codes, making this marking undeterminable

types.necessity: L1.lifecycle-mutates-outcome names status as one of the outcome facts that changes as a trade moves through its life (pending, submitted, completed, cancelled); a dedicated value is indispensable to express that fact, replaced by a later report rather than kept beside it.
types.parallel_assumption: Credible while the brokerage's own status coding names the trade's current lifecycle stage on every report.
types.review_trigger: a trade report carries no determinable status value

types.necessity: L1.lifecycle-mutates-outcome names executed price as one of the outcome facts that changes through a trade's life; a dedicated value is indispensable to express that specific fact, distinct from any bid or requested price.
types.parallel_assumption: Credible while the brokerage records a single executed-price value per trade report, replaced rather than accumulated.
types.review_trigger: a trade report carries more than one executed-price value, or the value recorded does not represent an executed price

types.necessity: L1.lifecycle-mutates-outcome names fees as one of the outcome facts that changes through a trade's life; a dedicated value is indispensable to express that specific fact, distinct from commission and tax.
types.parallel_assumption: Credible while the brokerage records a single fees value per trade report, replaced rather than accumulated.
types.review_trigger: a trade report carries more than one fees value

types.necessity: L1.lifecycle-mutates-outcome names commission as one of the outcome facts that changes through a trade's life; a dedicated value is indispensable to express that specific fact, distinct from fees and tax.
types.parallel_assumption: Credible while the brokerage records a single commission value per trade report, replaced rather than accumulated.
types.review_trigger: a trade report carries more than one commission value

types.necessity: L1.lifecycle-mutates-outcome names tax as one of the outcome facts that changes through a trade's life; a dedicated value is indispensable to express that specific fact, distinct from fees and commission.
types.parallel_assumption: Credible while the brokerage records a single tax value per trade report, replaced rather than accumulated.
types.review_trigger: a trade report carries more than one tax value

types.necessity: L1.lifecycle-mutates-outcome names quantity as one of the outcome facts that changes through a trade's life; a dedicated value is indispensable to express that specific fact.
types.parallel_assumption: Credible while the brokerage records a single quantity value per trade report, replaced rather than accumulated.
types.review_trigger: a trade report carries no determinable quantity value

entities.grain: one row per trade, identified by trade_number, updated in place by later reports that change its outcome facts and never change the frozen placement-moment ownership reference
entities.necessity: L1.identity requires a trade to be the same persistent identified thing across every report of it, not a new trade each time. L1.lifecycle-mutates-outcome requires that a later report of the same trade update its outcome (status, executed price, fees, commission, tax, quantity) in place. L1.attribution-at-placement requires that a trade's ownership, once established at placement, is never moved by a later change to the account or customer, and that nothing the trade created is moved either. Together these entail exactly one row per identified trade, updated in place by later reports, holding a portion frozen at first encounter beside a portion that mutates -- the incremental_by_identity history kind, not versioned (which would keep every report as a separate dated statement) and not append_by_identity (which would treat every report as a new, unrelated event).
entities.parallel_assumption: Credible while every raw.trade_cdc row for the same t_id is understood to be a later report about that same trade rather than a distinct trade reusing the number.
entities.review_trigger: a later trade_cdc row for a known trade_number is found to describe what the business considers a different trade
entities.note: This entity's frozen portion now carries the full reference L1.attribution-at-placement describes: which account (owning_account_number), which of that account's dated statements (owning_account_effective_from, as of placed_at), and through that statement, which customer (owning_customer_number) -- see sg.placement-moment. L1.placement-moment also calls for marking a trade first_seen_late when its first-encountered report is not the trade's true earliest lifecycle report, so the ownership it fixes can be reviewed. This model does not derive that marker: chain/anchors/sources-v1.json anchors no meaning for raw.trade_cdc's cdc_flag values or for t_st_id's lifecycle-stage codes, and detecting that a first-encountered report looks like it skipped earlier stages would require assigning meaning to codes the anchors do not define, which is a question for authority, not a derivation this job can make. Left as a note per this cycle's authority rather than modeled.

attributes.name: trade_number
attributes.necessity: L1.identity requires a value that identifies which trade a report is about and stays the same across every later report of that trade; this attribute carries the identity type for exactly that purpose.
attributes.parallel_assumption: Credible while the brokerage's trade number is stable and unique per trade.
attributes.review_trigger: two reports with different trade_number values are claimed to be about the same trade, or vice versa

attributes.name: owning_account_number
attributes.necessity: L1.attribution-at-placement requires a trade to belong to the account it was placed under and forbids a later change from moving it; this attribute names that account, set once at first encounter and never replaced by a later report.
attributes.parallel_assumption: Credible while the account a trade is placed under is settled at the trade's first-encountered report; whether a later report could legitimately correct it is not addressed by the clause and is not assumed here.
attributes.review_trigger: a later report of a known trade_number names an account different from the one recorded at first encounter

attributes.name: placed_at
attributes.necessity: L1.placement-moment requires placement to be the moment stated by the earliest report of the trade the brokerage holds, in that report's own time; this attribute carries that moment, set once at first encounter and never replaced by a later report.
attributes.parallel_assumption: Credible while the trade's first-encountered report states its own event time.
attributes.review_trigger: a trade's first-encountered report has no determinable event time

attributes.name: owning_account_effective_from
attributes.necessity: L1.attribution-at-placement requires the account to be referenced as it stood at placement, not merely named; together with owning_account_number, this attribute completes the (account_number, effective_from) pair that identifies the specific account statement in effect at placed_at, per L1.as-of's 'latest statement that took effect at or before' the queried moment.
attributes.parallel_assumption: Credible while the upstream logical.account entity carries a statement of this trade's owning account with an effective_from at or before placed_at; not yet resolvable where the correct statement is one of ownership-history's own deferred CDC-sourced account statements.
attributes.review_trigger: no logical.account statement of the owning account has an effective_from at or before placed_at, or more than one candidate ties for latest

attributes.name: owning_customer_number
attributes.necessity: L1.attribution-at-placement requires that, through the account, the trade also belongs to the customer as that customer stood at the same moment; this attribute carries that customer directly from the same account statement owning_account_number and owning_account_effective_from already pin, so it can never name a customer inconsistent with that statement.
attributes.parallel_assumption: Credible while the account statement pinned by owning_account_number and owning_account_effective_from has a resolvable owning_customer_number.
attributes.review_trigger: the account statement this trade's ownership pins has no resolvable owning_customer_number

attributes.name: first_seen_late

derivation.rule: true when the trade's first-encountered raw.trade_cdc report (the row with the smallest (batch_date, cdc_dsn) for that t_id, per trade_code_meanings.report_order) carries a t_st_id other than PNDG, the first status in trade_code_meanings.status_order; false when it is PNDG. Not received from any source; computed once, at first encounter, by comparing that report's own status against the anchored lifecycle order, per L1.placement-moment's definition of a trade first seen late.

attributes.necessity: L1.placement-moment requires a trade whose first-encountered report is not its true earliest lifecycle report to be marked first seen late, so the ownership placement fixes can be reviewed; using the anchored trade_code_meanings.status_order (PNDG, SBMT, CMPT), a first-encountered report whose status is not PNDG -- the order's first status -- is exactly such a trade (SBMT for a trade never seen pending; CMPT or CNCL for a trade never seen submitted). L1.attribution-at-placement requires this marking, once made, to be fixed at first encounter and not reconsidered by a later report.
attributes.parallel_assumption: Credible while trade_code_meanings.status_order and terminal_status_codes exhaustively enumerate a trade's lifecycle statuses (PNDG, SBMT, CMPT, CNCL) and every trade report carries one of them, and while report_order's (batch_date, cdc_dsn) ordering correctly identifies the first-encountered report; if the business states a status outside this enumeration, or an ordering other than file production order, this derivation must be revisited.
attributes.review_trigger: a trade's first-encountered report carries a status outside {PNDG, SBMT, CMPT, CNCL}

attributes.name: status
attributes.necessity: L1.lifecycle-mutates-outcome requires a trade's outcome, including its status, to change as it moves through its life and requires a later report to update that fact; this attribute carries status directly and is replaced by each later report.
attributes.parallel_assumption: Credible while every trade report carries a determinable lifecycle status (pending, submitted, completed, or cancelled).
attributes.review_trigger: a trade report carries no determinable status

attributes.name: executed_price
attributes.necessity: L1.lifecycle-mutates-outcome requires a trade's outcome, including its executed price, to change as it moves through its life and requires a later report to update that fact; this attribute carries executed price directly and is replaced by each later report.
attributes.parallel_assumption: Credible while a trade report supplies its own executed-price fact once the trade has executed; a report of a trade that has not yet executed may carry no executed price yet, which the clause does not forbid.
attributes.review_trigger: a trade report whose status the business considers executed or completed carries no executed price

attributes.name: fees
attributes.necessity: L1.lifecycle-mutates-outcome requires a trade's outcome, including its fees, to change as it moves through its life and requires a later report to update that fact; this attribute carries fees directly and is replaced by each later report.
attributes.parallel_assumption: Credible while a trade report supplies its own fees fact once determinable; a report of a trade not yet executed may carry no fees value yet, which the clause does not forbid.
attributes.review_trigger: a trade report whose status the business considers executed or completed carries no fees value

attributes.name: commission
attributes.necessity: L1.lifecycle-mutates-outcome requires a trade's outcome, including its commission, to change as it moves through its life and requires a later report to update that fact; this attribute carries commission directly and is replaced by each later report.
attributes.parallel_assumption: Credible while a trade report supplies its own commission fact once determinable; a report of a trade not yet executed may carry no commission value yet, which the clause does not forbid.
attributes.review_trigger: a trade report whose status the business considers executed or completed carries no commission value

attributes.name: tax
attributes.necessity: L1.lifecycle-mutates-outcome requires a trade's outcome, including its tax, to change as it moves through its life and requires a later report to update that fact; this attribute carries tax directly and is replaced by each later report.
attributes.parallel_assumption: Credible while a trade report supplies its own tax fact once determinable; a report of a trade not yet executed may carry no tax value yet, which the clause does not forbid.
attributes.review_trigger: a trade report whose status the business considers executed or completed carries no tax value

attributes.name: quantity
attributes.necessity: L1.lifecycle-mutates-outcome requires a trade's outcome, including its quantity, to change as it moves through its life and requires a later report to update that fact; this attribute carries quantity directly and is replaced by each later report.
attributes.parallel_assumption: Credible while every trade report carries a determinable quantity, from the moment it is placed onward.
attributes.review_trigger: a trade report carries no determinable quantity

handoffs.necessity: L1.identity requires the trade's own number as its identity; raw.trade_cdc carries t_id as the brokerage's trade number on every row reporting that trade, including its first-encountered row and every later report.
handoffs.parallel_assumption: Credible while t_id values in this file are the brokerage's real trade numbers and not reused for different trades.
handoffs.review_trigger: a t_id value in this file is found reassigned to a different trade

handoffs.necessity: L1.attribution-at-placement requires the trade's own account be named and fixed at first encounter; raw.trade_cdc's t_ca_id is the brokerage's own recorded account number on the trade's first-encountered report, and this handoff takes that value only, never a later report's t_ca_id, per the clause's 'do not move a trade that was already placed.'
handoffs.parallel_assumption: Credible while t_ca_id on a trade's first-encountered report names the account the trade was placed under.
handoffs.review_trigger: t_ca_id is found to record something other than the trade's owning account, or to change across reports of the same trade

handoffs.necessity: L1.placement-moment requires placement to be the moment stated by the earliest report of the trade the brokerage holds, in that report's own time; raw.trade_cdc's t_dts is that report's own recorded time, and this handoff takes it only from the trade's first-encountered report, never a later one.
handoffs.parallel_assumption: Credible while t_dts on a trade's first-encountered report is the report's own stated time of that event, not a receipt or batch-load time.
handoffs.review_trigger: t_dts is found to record something other than the report's own event time

handoffs.necessity: L1.attribution-at-placement requires the trade's ownership reference to name the account as it stood at the moment of placement; L1.as-of defines that answer as the latest statement that took effect at or before the queried moment. This handoff selects, among the upstream ownership-history statements of this trade's owning_account_number, the one whose effective_from is the latest at or before placed_at, and freezes that effective_from as the second half of the (account_number, effective_from) reference identifying the specific account statement -- not the account's current statement.
handoffs.parallel_assumption: Credible while the upstream logical.account entity carries a resolvable statement of this trade's owning account with an effective_from at or before placed_at.
handoffs.review_trigger: no logical.account statement of the owning account has an effective_from at or before placed_at, or more than one candidate ties for latest

handoffs.necessity: L1.attribution-at-placement requires that, through the account, the trade also belongs to the customer as that customer stood at the same moment; the account statement already pinned by owning_account_number and owning_account_effective_from carries, as its own owning_customer_number, exactly that customer. This handoff freezes that same value directly off the pinned statement rather than performing an independent as-of lookup, so the customer named can never be inconsistent with the account statement this trade's ownership pins.
handoffs.parallel_assumption: Credible wherever the account statement pinned by owning_account_number and owning_account_effective_from itself has a resolvable owning_customer_number.
handoffs.review_trigger: the account statement pinned by owning_account_number and owning_account_effective_from has no resolvable owning_customer_number

handoffs.necessity: L1.lifecycle-mutates-outcome requires a later report of a trade to update its status; raw.trade_cdc's t_st_id is the brokerage's own recorded lifecycle-status value on each report of the trade.
handoffs.parallel_assumption: Credible while t_st_id on a trade_cdc row names the trade's lifecycle status as of that report.
handoffs.review_trigger: t_st_id is found to record something other than the trade's lifecycle status

handoffs.necessity: L1.lifecycle-mutates-outcome requires a later report to update the trade's executed price; raw.trade_cdc's t_trade_price is the brokerage's own recorded executed-price value on each report, distinct from t_bid_price, which records the price at which the trade was requested rather than executed and this job does not hand off.
handoffs.parallel_assumption: Credible while t_trade_price on a trade_cdc row names the price at which the trade actually executed, as of that report.
handoffs.review_trigger: t_trade_price is found to record a requested price rather than an executed price

handoffs.necessity: L1.lifecycle-mutates-outcome requires a later report to update the trade's fees; raw.trade_cdc's t_chrg is the brokerage's own recorded charge value on each report, the fees fact the clause names.
handoffs.parallel_assumption: Credible while t_chrg on a trade_cdc row names the fees the brokerage charges on the trade, as of that report.
handoffs.review_trigger: t_chrg is found to record something other than fees

handoffs.necessity: L1.lifecycle-mutates-outcome requires a later report to update the trade's commission; raw.trade_cdc's t_comm is the brokerage's own recorded commission value on each report.
handoffs.parallel_assumption: Credible while t_comm on a trade_cdc row names the commission charged on the trade, as of that report.
handoffs.review_trigger: t_comm is found to record something other than commission

handoffs.necessity: L1.lifecycle-mutates-outcome requires a later report to update the trade's tax; raw.trade_cdc's t_tax is the brokerage's own recorded tax value on each report.
handoffs.parallel_assumption: Credible while t_tax on a trade_cdc row names the tax owed on the trade, as of that report.
handoffs.review_trigger: t_tax is found to record something other than tax

handoffs.necessity: L1.lifecycle-mutates-outcome requires a later report to update the trade's quantity; raw.trade_cdc's t_qty is the brokerage's own recorded quantity value on each report.
handoffs.parallel_assumption: Credible while t_qty on a trade_cdc row names the trade's quantity, as of that report.
handoffs.review_trigger: t_qty is found to record something other than quantity

invariants.statement: For any trade_number, every raw.trade_cdc report of that trade carries the same t_ca_id as the trade's first-encountered report; owning_account_number is set once at first encounter and is never replaced by a later report.
invariants.necessity: L1.attribution-at-placement states directly that later changes do not move a trade that was already placed; this invariant is the restatement of that requirement over the account a trade is recorded against.
invariants.parallel_assumption: Holds while raw.trade_cdc never legitimately reassigns a trade to a different account after its first report; a contradiction would indicate a data error or an unaddressed business rule, not a value this attribute should adopt.
invariants.review_trigger: a later raw.trade_cdc report of a known trade_number carries a t_ca_id different from the one recorded at first encounter

invariants.statement: For any trade_number, placed_at, owning_account_effective_from, and owning_customer_number are each set once -- from the trade's first-encountered report and the account statement resolved as of that report's own time -- and are never replaced by a later report of the same trade.
invariants.necessity: L1.placement-moment fixes placement to the earliest held report's own time, and L1.attribution-at-placement states directly that later changes do not move a trade that was already placed; this invariant is the restatement of that requirement over the placement-moment reference attributes.
invariants.parallel_assumption: Holds while a later raw.trade_cdc report of a known trade never carries an earlier event time than the one already recorded as placed_at.
invariants.review_trigger: a later raw.trade_cdc report of a known trade_number carries an event time earlier than its recorded placed_at, or any of placed_at, owning_account_effective_from, owning_customer_number is found replaced after first encounter

invariants.statement: For any trade_number, a later raw.trade_cdc report of that same trade replaces status, executed_price, fees, commission, tax, and quantity with its newly reported values on the same row; the trade_number itself is never replaced.
invariants.necessity: L1.lifecycle-mutates-outcome states directly that a later report of the same trade updates the outcome; this invariant is the restatement of that update-in-place requirement over the six named outcome facts.
invariants.parallel_assumption: Holds while every raw.trade_cdc row for a given t_id is a later report about that same trade rather than an unrelated new trade reusing the number.
invariants.review_trigger: two raw.trade_cdc rows with the same t_id are found to disagree in a way that suggests they describe different trades

invariants.statement: This model defines no handoff sourced from a labeled constructed scenario for the trade entity, because chain/anchors/sources-v1.json anchors no ce.trade_* source; every trade statement this model can produce originates from raw.trade_cdc alone.
invariants.necessity: L1.constructed-scenarios requires a constructed scenario to be labeled wherever it appears and never mixed into received records; with no constructed trade source anchored, this job has no mechanism that could introduce an unlabeled constructed fact into the trade entity, satisfying the clause vacuously for this job as it stands.
invariants.parallel_assumption: Credible while sources-v1.json continues to anchor no labeled constructed source for trades; if one is added, this invariant and the model must be revisited.
invariants.review_trigger: sources-v1.json gains a ce.trade_* entry, or a trade statement is found to originate from anything other than raw.trade_cdc

sufficiency_groups.coverage_claim: logical.trade's history kind, incremental_by_identity, is the direct consequence of L1.identity (a trade is a persistent identified thing; a later report about the same trade number is the same trade, not a new one), L1.lifecycle-mutates-outcome (a later report updates outcome facts on this same row), and L1.attribution-at-placement (the trade's ownership, once established at placement, is never moved by a later report about the account or customer) -- together these entail one row per trade_number, updated in place, holding a frozen portion beside a mutable portion. The frozen portion's account-identity component is owning_account_number: raw.trade_cdc's t_ca_id, taken only from the trade's first-encountered report and never replaced by a later one, which inv.trade_owning_account_frozen restates directly. This is the part of L1.attribution-at-placement that names which account a trade belongs to, fixed at first encounter; the remaining part -- which dated statement of that account, and through it which customer, stood as of the moment of placement -- is now resolved by L1.placement-moment and covered by sg.placement-moment instead, since that is the more specific claim. This group's own scope is limited to the entity's shape and the account-identity portion.

L1.placement-moment fixes placement to the moment stated by the trade's earliest held report, in that report's own time: placed_at, handed off from raw.trade_cdc's t_dts with selector first_encounter_only, carries exactly that moment, frozen. L1.attribution-at-placement requires the trade's ownership to reference the account (and through it the customer) as they stood at that moment, not the account's current statement; L1.as-of defines that answer as the upstream logical.account statement whose effective_from is the latest at or before placed_at. owning_account_effective_from, handed off from logical.account.effective_from with selector as_of_event_time, completes the (account_number, effective_from) pair with owning_account_number (sg.trade-shape) that identifies that exact statement. owning_customer_number is handed off directly from that same pinned statement's own logical.account.owning_customer_number, so it can never name a customer inconsistent with it, satisfying the 'and through it the customer' half of the clause. inv.trade_placement_reference_frozen restates that all three attributes are set once, at first encounter, and never replaced. L1.placement-moment also calls for a first_seen_late marker distinguishing a trade whose first-encountered report is not its true earliest lifecycle report; this job does not derive that marker because sources-v1.json anchors no meaning for raw.trade_cdc's cdc_flag or t_st_id codes that would let this job detect a skipped earlier report without inventing code meanings the anchors do not state -- left as a note on logical.trade rather than modeled or blocked by a question, per this cycle's authority.

Every raw.trade_cdc row carries t_id, the brokerage's own trade number, handed off unchanged into trade_number with the identity mutation role; because this value is identical across every CDC row reporting the same trade, no later report ever produces a 'different' trade, satisfying L1.identity's persistence requirement for the trade entity.

L1.lifecycle-mutates-outcome enumerates exactly six outcome facts -- status, executed price, fees, commission, tax, quantity -- that change as a trade moves through its life. Each is handed off from raw.trade_cdc's own field for that fact (t_st_id, t_trade_price, t_chrg, t_comm, t_tax, t_qty respectively), typed mutable, and a later CDC row for the same trade_number replaces each with its newly reported value, which inv.trade_outcome_updates_in_place restates directly. All six facts the clause names are covered by a member of this group; the clause names no others.

chain/anchors/sources-v1.json anchors no labeled constructed source for trades (only ce.account_changes exists, and that is for accounts); this job therefore has no handoff that could mix an unlabeled constructed fact into the trade entity, and inv.trade_not_constructed restates that every trade statement this model can produce originates from raw.trade_cdc alone, satisfying L1.constructed-scenarios' labeling and non-mixing requirement vacuously for this job as it stands. Because owning_account_effective_from and owning_customer_number (sg.placement-moment) are references to the upstream account statement, not copies of its facts, a trade whose ownership pins a statement sourced from ce.account_changes carries that statement's own provenance label reachable through the reference; this job introduces no separate, unlabeled copy that could obscure it.

holes.question: L1.placement-moment now settles placement; this hole now covers only completion: which moment counts as 'when it completed' when a later report of a trade arrives without its full history? This job does not model a completed-at moment, so nothing here is currently blocked by it, but it is carried because a future completion-timing attribute would need it answered.

Trades appear on accounts the brokerage recorded as closed years earlier. Is that a data error, a reopening the records omit, or does a closed account still own trades? Until answered, a trade's ownership reference (once resolvable) may point to an account statement whose closed status this job cannot verify against the trade's own later activity.

Does a change recorded in an incremental account or customer change file take effect at the file's batch date, or at some other moment? Until answered, some account statements this job's owning_account_effective_from and owning_customer_number handoffs would need to resolve a trade's as-of ownership against remain unavailable, per ownership-history's own deferred handoffs from raw.account_cdc and raw.customer_cdc.
